criteria.criterion: With ticket held by session A, `rebar show <id>` and `rebar comment <id> ...` run as session B print a `WARN:` line naming holder `A` to stderr, with unchanged stdout and exit code 0
Negative control: the same commands as session A print no `WARN:` line
`rebar list` and `rebar ready` as session B print no cross-session `WARN:` line even with A's `in_progress` ticket present
`rebar show <id>` with `REBAR_SESSION_ID` unset prints no `WARN:` line
`rebar link <id1> <id2>` as session B, with A holding `id1`, prints a single `WARN:` naming holder `A` computed for the primary `id1` only
The stderr emit is best-effort: when `cross_session_warning_for` raises, the command still completes normally and unwarned
`docs/user-guide.md` documents the CLI stderr warning and the bulk exclusion (checked: `grep -n "another session" docs/user-guide.md` matches)

findings.criterion: `docs/user-guide.md` documents the CLI stderr warning and the bulk exclusion (checked: `grep -n "another session" docs/user-guide.md` matches).
findings.detail: The acceptance criterion specifies that `grep -n "another session" docs/user-guide.md` must match. A search for the literal string "another session" in docs/user-guide.md returned no matches. While docs/user-guide.md does contain a WARN-related line at line 437 (found via search for "WARN"), the specific phrase "another session" required by the acceptance criterion's grep check is absent from the file.
findings.remediation: Add the phrase "another session" to the cross-session warning documentation section in docs/user-guide.md so that `grep -n "another session" docs/user-guide.md` produces a match.
findings.title: docs/user-guide.md missing "another session" phrase

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[non-codebase]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
